title: Bali tourist levy
whoPays: International tourists visiting Bali. The same portal has an exemption application.
howToPay: Online through the Bali provincial government's Love Bali portal.

legal_source.name: Love Bali (Bali Provincial Government), Bali Provincial Regulation No. 2 of 2025 amending Regional Regulation No. 6 of 2023

title: International Tourist Tax
amountText: JPY 3,000 per departure from Japan (JPY 1,000 if you depart on an eligible ticket issued on or before 30 June 2026)
whoPays: International tourists leaving Japan by aircraft or ship, whatever their purpose or nationality. Exempt include transit passengers who leave Japan within 24 hours after entry and passengers under the age of 2.
howToPay: Airlines and cruise lines collect it from their passengers.
notes: The same page's introduction still mentions JPY 1,000; its tax-rate section gives JPY 3,000 with the transitional rule.

legal_source.name: National Tax Agency, International Tourist Tax: basic knowledge

title: Kenyan Government inbound travel health insurance
amountText: Up to USD 44 per person, covering up to 3 months with multiple entries
whoPays: Non-Kenyans visiting for less than 3 months (tourism, business, conferences, family visits), each traveller with their own policy, including travellers who don't need an eTA. Your own travel insurance doesn't replace it. Exempt: Kenyan citizens and residents, citizens of East African Community states, asylum seekers, holders of diplomatic, official and service passports, some crew, and transit passengers who don't enter Kenya.
howToPay: Travellers who need an eTA are asked to buy it during the eTA application; others buy it on the eCitizen insurance portal.

legal_source.name: Government of Kenya, eCitizen Inbound Travel Health Insurance

title: Inbound Travel Insurance (mainland Tanzania)
amountText: USD 44 per visitor, valid up to 92 days
whoPays: Foreign visitors entering through mainland Tanzania (Government Notice No. 256 of 2026). Visitors entering through Zanzibar buy theirs from the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation instead.
howToPay: From the National Insurance Corporation (NIC). The Ministry of Finance advises buying it before you travel.

legal_source.name: Ministry of Finance public notice on Inbound Travel Insurance (GN No. 256 of 2026), published by the Embassy of Tanzania in Italy

title: Visitor health insurance
amountText: QAR 50 for a 30-day policy, the minimum length (other visas vary)
whoPays: Visitors who need a visa before arriving: the visa isn't granted until you've bought it. Visitors eligible for a visa on arrival are exempt for their first 30 days, but must buy it to stay longer.
howToPay: From an insurer registered with the Ministry of Public Health, through the ministry's website, before arriving.

legal_source.name: Ministry of Public Health, Health Financing and Insurance Department FAQs

title: Galápagos protected areas entry fee
amountText: US$200 for foreign tourists over 12, US$100 under 12; nationals of Andean Community or Mercosur countries pay US$100 and US$50
whoPays: Foreign tourists entering the Galápagos protected areas (Provincial Ordinance No. 001-CGREG-30-06-2025).
howToPay: Park rangers collect it at Baltra and San Cristóbal airports.

legal_source.name: Galápagos National Park Directorate, Tributo de ingreso (Ordenanza Provincial No. 001-CGREG-30-06-2025)

title: Galápagos Transit Control Card (TCT)
whoPays: Visitors flying to the Galápagos. Keep the card until you leave the islands (stays of up to 2 months).
howToPay: At the Galápagos Government Council office at Quito or Guayaquil airport, before checking in with your airline.

legal_source.name: Galápagos National Park Directorate, Información de interés para la llegada a las islas

title: Tourist Card
whoPays: Visitors entering for tourism without a consular visa. The source lists exempt categories.
howToPay: Since 25 April 2018 it's included in every air ticket issued outside the Dominican Republic. Arriving by land or sea, you buy it at the tax authority's (DGII) points of sale there.

legal_source.name: Dirección General de Impuestos Internos (DGII), Sobre la Tarjeta de Turista

title: Visitor fee (Derecho de No Residente, DNR)
whoPays: Foreigners arriving by air as visitors without permission to do paid work (tourists and business visitors). Crew on scheduled international flights staying no more than seven days don't pay.
howToPay: By Visa or Mastercard card, at a bank counter with INM's help sheet, or by electronic transfer. INM staff never accept cash.
notes: Set by Article 8, section I of Mexico's Federal Fees Law (Ley Federal de Derechos). INM's air-entry table doesn't say whether airlines include the fee in the ticket price, and the land and sea entry tables weren't read.

legal_source.name: Instituto Nacional de Migración: Tabla de costos de pago de derechos, internación vía aérea 2026 (Ley Federal de Derechos)

title: Airport migration services fee on departure (DSM)
whoPays: Passengers on international flights leaving Mexico.
notes: Set by Article 12 of Mexico's Federal Fees Law (Ley Federal de Derechos). INM's table doesn't say how it is collected or whether airlines include it in the ticket price.

legal_source.name: Instituto Nacional de Migración: Tabla de costos de pago de derechos, internación vía aérea 2026 (Ley Federal de Derechos)

title: International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy (IVL)
amountText: NZD 100, each time you request an NZeTA or apply for a visa that includes it
whoPays: Many visitors: it's charged with the NZeTA and with visitor, student, working holiday and some work visas. Not charged on an Australian or New Zealand passport, a passport from many Pacific Island nations, to transit passengers arriving at and leaving from Auckland International Airport, to holders of a New Zealand resident visa or an Australian Resident Visa, or with a Business Visitor Visa or APEC business travel card.
howToPay: Paid with the NZeTA request or the visa application. It isn't refunded, even if the application is declined.
notes: Immigration New Zealand's online tool, Fees, decision times and where to apply, confirms which other visa holders don't pay and which Pacific passports are exempt.

legal_source.name: Immigration New Zealand: Paying the International Visitor Levy
